findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: A few cartons of milks were stored overnight in the standing cooler that wasn't functioning properly. Milk cartons were discarded. See violation #33 for further details. Be sure that TCS food items stored in cold holding units are maintained at 41F or less to ensure proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The 2 door standing cooler in the kitchen area was observed with an ambient temperature of 59F. The temperature gauge on the outside of the cooler read 60F. Items such as but not limited to cheese quesadillas, salsa, lettuce, and fruit were recently placed inside the unit. The items were pulled from the unit and placed into the walk in cooler. Food items stored in the cooler overnight were discarded (cartons of milks). Maintenance was contacted to service the cooler. After servicing the cooler, a probe thermometer placed inside of the unit read 40F, correcting the violation. Ensure that cold holding equipment is sufficient enough to maintain proper cold holding temperatures of 41F or less.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.
